noveltyJustification: Six findings are new; the four-list drift pattern is confirmed on a second hub, and the mcp stage-one/stage-two gap and the standalone leaf-manifest model are new evidence.
ruledOut: Treating the mcp hub as a copy of the CLI hub
Treating DEFAULT_RESOURCE=[] and DEFAULT_RESOURCE=path as a contradiction

label: Stage one routes mcp-obsidian on health, Iconic, Excalidraw and Minimal-theme classes, but ROUTER.md has no stage-two intent for them, so those requests reach the mode and then defer.

mcp-tooling repeats the four-list vocabulary pattern and drifts the same way: 6 chrome, 5 click-up, 6 obsidian, 4 aside, 1 notion, 4 figma, 2 refero and 4 mobbin registry aliases are absent from ROUTER.md; only magicpath matches exactly.
mcp packets state the same fallback-only default contract as the hub router, so the contract is restated ten times but agrees; the CLI hub's disagreement is a packet defect, not a hub pattern.

mcp-code-mode is the working standalone-skill model: no mode-registry and no hub router, yet a typed leaf projection through leaf-manifest.json, leaf-manifest.config.json and leaf-aliases.json regenerated by generate-leaf-manifest.cjs.
mcp-code-mode's DEFAULT_RESOURCE is also its only ALWAYS entry, so the if-not-loaded fallback branch is dead unless the file is missing.

The leaf-manifest regeneration instruction is actionable in mcp-code-mode, which names the script and the --check contract, and unactionable in mcp-tooling, which says only to use the canonical metadata command.

Readability splits: mcp-tooling's hub is 152 lines with a 17-line routing section, while mcp-code-mode puts 155 lines of routing (134 of Python) before its first instruction and carries a 972-character paragraph at line 62.
